title: Post-Incident Reconstruction & SIEM Correlation Template — credential exfiltration
content:
Purpose:
This document is a templated reconstruction and correlation checklist for security postmortems with a focus on suspected credential exfiltration and downstream SIEM correlation. Use as the canonical run-through for assembling a timeline, validating evidence completeness, and deriving mitigation actions for RBAC/audit gaps.

Scope and when to use this template:
- Use when: authentication anomalies, mass token misuse, or suspicious outbound data movement tied to service/robot accounts are suspected.
- Out of scope: purely availability incidents (DDoS) unless accompanied by authentication/authorization breaches.

Executive summary (to be populated first):
- One-line summary of what happened
- Impact (customers, internal systems, data categories)
- Detection vector (alert name, SIEM rule id or telemetry)
- Business impact estimate (approx. MAUs affected, data types)

Primary contacts and escalation:
- Incident lead: <name> (security on-call)
- Engineering liaison: <name> (affected service owner)
- Legal/Privacy: <name>
- Communications: <name>
- For criminal matters: coordinate with InfoSec manager before contacting law enforcement

Initial containment checklist (first 2 hours):
- Rotate exposed credentials or disable compromised service accounts. Note exact keys rotated and timestamps.
- Revoke affected tokens and trigger revocation endpoints where supported.
- Apply temporary deny policy in RBAC v2 for implicated principals (document ACL change IDs).
- Snap ephemeral host images and isolate impacted VPC/subnets for forensic imaging.

Forensic evidence collection checklist (mandatory items):
- SIEM export slice: Collect time-bounded export (start/end) of ingestion for: auth events, token issuance, token introspection, service account activities, API key use. Exports should be in raw JSON/NDJSON.
- Audit logs (control plane): Export full audit trail for IAM service, RBAC change events, and key-management operations. Fields to verify: timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_id, resource_type, request_id, outcome, source_ip, user_agent.
- Application logs: Pull the app logs for the implicated service for the same time window including request_id tracing.
- Network captures: If available, pull relevant pcap or flow logs for egress destinations tied to suspected exfiltration.
- Host snapshots: MD5/sha256 for key binaries, process lists, memory dumps where feasible.
- Chain-of-custody notes: who pulled each artifact, time collected, where stored (S3 bucket ID with restricted ACL), checksum.

Audit log schema quick map (fields to prioritize):
- ts (ISO8601 string)
- event_id (UUID)
- actor.id (short principal identifier)
- actor.type (user, service_account, robot)
- actor.subject (email or principal name)
- action (string: iam.grant, auth.token.issue, auth.token.revoke, kms.encrypt, kms.decrypt, object.read, object.write)
- resource.id
- resource.type
- outcome (success|failure|warning)
- src.ip
- user_agent
- request_id
- trace_id
Note: Some downstream systems flatten actor.* into actor_id, actor_type. Map both variants when correlating.

SIEM export and correlation steps (practical):
1) Identify alert window (t0,t1) and pull exports for +30m before and +2h after.
2) Export raw SIEM events (NDJSON preferred) and store in evidence bucket.
3) Run automated correlation script (see linked_artifacts) to join events on request_id and trace_id.
4) Build scatter timeline: primary auth events, token issuance, high-volume data reads/writes, egress connections.
5) Tag events with derived fields: suspect_principal, likely_exfil_destination, confirmed_token_use.

IR timeline template (populate each row):
- timestamp_iso | source_system | event_type | principal | resource | request_id | short_summary | evidence_hash_or_path
Example row:
- 2025-10-11T03:42:12Z | auth-service | token.issue | svc-payments-robot | /v1/keys | f2d4a1.. | long-lived token issued for svc-payments-robot | s3://evidence/siem/exp1.ndjson#sha256:...

RBAC v2 specific checks (what to look for):
- Recent policy rollouts: list rollout_id and timestamp for last 30d; inspect diffs for inadvertent allow additions.
- Bindings to wildcard principals or broad roles (e.g., role:infra-admin assigned to group:everyone).
- Service account impersonation chains in audit logs (actor=deployment-tool impersonated svc account).
- Policy evaluation failures or legacy rule overrides.
- Are temporary elevation tokens issued? Check token TTLs and issuance method.

Evidence automation notes (quick-win scripts and cautions):
- Use automation only for metadata extraction (hashes, list of event_ids, time windows). Avoid scripts that mutate live logs or rotate keys automatically unless run under an approved on-call Safety mode.
- Script checklist included in repo: security-scripts/evidence-extract (PR 42) — extracts raw SIEM slice, enriches actor metadata via internal identity graph, and zips artifacts with checksums.

Containment -> Eradication -> Recovery playbook (practical steps):
- Containment: isolate principals, revoke sessions, apply deny rules.
- Eradication: remove backdoors, clean compromised images, rotate keys and secrets used on affected machines, update deployment artifacts to not reintroduce credentials.
- Recovery: re-deploy clean images, re-enable services in phased manner with audit log monitoring turned to high-sensitivity for first 72h.

Communication and legal preservation:
- Mark evidence with internal TLP and legal hold flags if sensitive customer data may be affected.
- Legal should be looped in before any external notifications.
- Prepare customer notification draft if PII or regulated data is involved; run through legal templates and Communication owner sign-off.

Root cause analysis prompts (to be answered during write-up):
- How did the principal obtain the credential? (misconfiguration, code leak, secret in repo, lateral movement)
- Which RBAC rule(s) enabled excessive access?
- Why didn't automated detection escalate earlier? (tuning, missing telemetry, blind spots)
- Which technical and process controls failed?

Action items and owners (example):
- Rotate all long-lived service tokens older than 90d — owner: infra-secrets (due: 2025-11-09)
- Add SIEM rule for abnormal token issuance patterns — owner: sec-analytics (due: 2025-11-05)
- Harden RBAC role inheritance tests in pre-prod pipeline — owner: platform-eng (due: 2025-11-16)

Postmortem write-up outline (deliverable sections):
- Summary and impact
- Detection and timeline (attach SIEM correlation artifacts)
- Root cause analysis
- Containment/eradication steps performed
- Monitoring and detection improvements planned
- Policy/process changes (incl. RBAC v2 adjustments)
- Owner-signed closure checklist

Appendix: quick forensic queries (examples to run against audit store)
- Find all token.issue events for principal X in last 7 days:
  query: \"action=\"auth.token.issue\" AND actor.subject=\"svc-payments-robot@redwood\" | sort ts desc\"
- Join token usage to object reads by request_id:
  query: \"source=siem_events | filter request_id IN (select request_id from source where action=\"auth.token.issue\") | where action IN (\"object.read\",\"object.write\")\"
- RBAC diffs in last 30d:
  query: \"source=audit | filter action=\"iam.policy.update\" AND ts >= now()-30d | fields rollout_id, diff_summary\"

Checklist for postmortem closure (all items must be Y/N + evidence link):
- Root cause identified and documented
- Action items assigned with deadlines
- SIEM correlation artifacts archived with checksums
- RBAC adjustments tested in staging and rolled to prod with canary
- Legal/comms sign-off on customer messaging

Notes and tips from prior incidents:
- Preserve raw SIEM NDJSON slices; derived dashboards are no substitute for raw events.
- When in doubt, collect more context (longer time window) — it’s cheap compared to missing the pivot.
- Avoid blanket revocations for high-availability service accounts without an emergency rollback plan.

Owner sign-off:
- Incident lead: ___________________  date: ____________
- Security manager: ________________  date: ____________

End of template.

Document history:
- 2025-10-12: template created by Avery Chen
- 2025-10-19: added RBAC v2 checklist and audit schema mapping (collab Priya Singh)
- 2025-11-02: SIEM export step clarifications and linked scripts updated (collab Diego Morales)
